speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) what is the process for reviewing and approving individual requests to exceed MediSave withdrawal limits; and (b) what criteria, documentation and exceptional circumstances are considered in such case-by-case applications for urgent medical needs.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Several of my residents have shared that the current limit of $300 is too low for their healthcare needs.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first is to ask the Minister of State whether patients and families are adequately informed of the option to apply for exemptions from MediSave withdrawal limits and what avenues exist for assistance in submitting these applications?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second question: how long on average does it take for individual applications that exceed MediSave withdrawal limits to be processed and whether interim relief is available for patients with urgent medical needs?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And my last question: whether there are sufficient safeguards to ensure that lower-income patients are not discouraged from applying for MediSave limit exemptions due to the administrative burden or complexity?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I can appreciate concerns from her residents, but I would like to highlight that in respect of her first point, within the public healthcare institutions, there are medical social workers who are embedded in the system and are ready and available to give guidance to the patients when they face difficulties in paying their bills.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would also like to highlight that beyond just the usage of MediSave, having exceptional circumstances where they can withdraw within the limits, there are also other sources of support, including access to MediFund, discretionary support in the hospitals, in the public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, that is a key point to note.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would encourage the patients to go and seek support from the medical social worker, because they may be able to then look at the slew of support that is available for the patients.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That would be prioritised and that would be something that the healthcare workers and the doctors and the nurses will ensure happen.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In the other part of the question, the Member asked about the timing needed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It really depends on the cases, because we do need to look at each case and the nuances and the reasons behind the application.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And the complexity of the case may matter, in terms of the timing as to how we come up with the outcomes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But I would just want to stress that there has been no situation where if they cannot afford the treatment, they do not get the treatment, because that is usually prioritised.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The last bit, the Member had asked about how do we ensure that those from low-income families are not prevented or discouraged from applying for exceptional withdrawal limits.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would say that no one is prevented or discouraged from applying for the exceptional limits.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, they should not hesitate to ask for help if they need to.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On a broader point, I just want to highlight that the first point is that MediSave is just one of the options for those who need support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There are other financial avenues available and I hope that patients are aware of that and would seek help from the medical social workers for that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The second point is, it is always tricky about MediSave.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The intention, the whole objective of MediSave is to ensure that you have enough for the big catastrophic events that happens.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And this typically happens later part in life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we need to find that balance of making sure that there is accessibility to its usage, but to also preserve it for healthcare needs in the future.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To that point, we do review it periodically to make sure that there are sufficient enhancements and support given.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, these are things that reflect that we do review this periodically and will enhance it where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just a follow-up question to the Senior Minister of State, with regard to the MediSave limits.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think some years ago, it was suggested by myself, whether the MediSave criteria for certain individuals could be loosened on the basis of how much they have in their MediSave accounts, particularly for seniors who, I am sure Member would appreciate, would visit at the meet-the-people sessions and say, "Look, we have got $40,000, $50,000 in our MediSave accounts and we just need a little bit more assistance", particularly, since these seniors have retired.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I am wondering whether the Ministry is prepared to exercise some flexibility in a more purposive way to ensure that some of these seniors can be allowed to use more of their MediSave monies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the question from the Leader of Opposition, I appreciate the sentiments, because I also do get those appeals from time to time.
I would suggest that the Member can surface it to the Ministry.
But we really have to look at the circumstances, the treatment, the costs as well as the balances in the MediSave.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I recognise that last September, MOH mentioned to a Parliamentary Question that you are looking to review these limits.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Many Singaporeans, including my residents in Ayer Rajah, have told me that they do not qualify for the subsidies because they are retired and they are seniors, but they are also unable to fork out the top-up to pay for their medical fees in cash because that would affect their daily living.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: With rising costs of living, it is difficult for them.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I am asking the Minister of State whether we have a timeline as to when the next review might be.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do the review periodically, as and when we are looking into it, and when we have reviewed something, we will make the announcements.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Members who wish to give feedback can also let us know.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We also need to understand that there are many different levers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There is the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), there is the MediFund in situations where they need it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And we may need to look at what are the different ways in which you can help support the particular individual.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But I am open to see if there are any further areas for which Members feel that there is a need of this.
